Perf Canary Bot: :rotating_light: Auto-rollback triggered (perf-canary)
- Service: hosted-inference
- Region: eu-west
- Model: rw-llama3-70b
- Cohort: canary-5% (kernel_mode=fp8)
- Metric: TTFT p95
- Baseline: 410ms
- Canary: 518ms (+26.3%)
- Window: 10m (n=612)
- Threshold profile: fp8_int8_ttft_tpot_v2
- Action: rolling back flag `runtime.fp8_attention_kernels` to previous stable
- Rollback id: pcb-77319

Rafael Mendes: seeing it. grabbing the dashboard + confirming rollback is actually applying in eu-west control plane.

Allison Grant: grafana slice w/ the tags: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/fp8-int8-canary/e2e-canary (set region=eu-west, model=rw-llama3-70b, kernel_mode=fp8)
TTFT p50 also shifted, TPOT looks flat. errors unchanged.

Rafael Mendes: control plane shows flag flip in progress (propagation ~2-3 min). watching request headers for `x-rw-kernel-mode` to confirm.

Marcus Reed: do we know if this is prefill-only? the last build had scheduler instrumentation for prefill/decode split; can you check the prefill queue depth histogram too?

Allison Grant: yep. prefill queue depth spikes correlate w/ the TTFT bump.
`queue_depth_prefill_p95` went from ~3 to ~11 during the window.

Julian Moore: pulling traces from the scheduler metrics panel. looks like more time in "prefill wait" not "prefill compute".
so kernel might be increasing batch formation time? or contention.

Yuki Sato: FYI we had a similar TTFT regression in eng-runtime thread when fp8 attention path gets selected for certain prompt-length regimes (launch overhead + interleaving). might be same shape bucket.

Rafael Mendes: rollback status: COMPLETE.
I’m now seeing kernel_mode baseline in sampled requests, TTFT trending down already.

Irene Choi: quick sanity: eu-west cluster `gpu-euw-03` is still on the older driver image (CUDA 12.3) unless the pin landed. could be contributing if fp8 path is more sensitive.

Vanessa Ortiz: +1, that cluster was on the exception list last week. we can drain canary traffic away from it if needed.

Hiro Tanaka: can someone paste the exact canary dimensions? model hash + container tag? want to make sure we’re not mixing runtime rc builds.

Allison Grant: from the canary metadata panel:
- runtime: 1.22.0-rc3
- image: redwood/runtime-serving:1.22.0-rc3-cuda12.4
- git: 3d91c7b
- model artifact: rw-llama3-70b@2026-02-24.2
- kernel_mode tag was `fp8_attention_v2`

Rafael Mendes: ok so it’s not a mixed rc. 
next steps per runbook: keep fp8 attention disabled in eu-west for this model until runtime signs off.
I’m setting a region+model override now (leaving other regions unchanged).

Sofia Ivanova: if queue depth is the main symptom, canary might be hitting a different concurrency mix than the harness. did anything change in eu-west load shaping today?

Rafael Mendes: not seeing load shaping changes. but we did have a small burst in eu-west around the same time (top customer batch job).
still, rollback should have absorbed it; TTFT was a step change at flag enable.

Neha Kapoor: please log the driver mismatch angle as an action item. if eu-west is on older driver, we shouldn’t be canarying fp8 kernels there.

Rafael Mendes: agreed.
Actions I’m taking:
1) keep override: `runtime.fp8_attention_kernels=off` for rw-llama3-70b in eu-west
2) create follow-up ticket for driver/CUDA parity requirement for canary regions
3) hand off perf regression triage to runtime w/ the dashboard links + exact window

Marcus Reed: can you also capture the before/after for `scheduler_interleave_ratio`? if fp8 attention changes compute time distribution, it can shift batching behavior.

Allison Grant: grabbed. interleave ratio moved from ~0.62 -> ~0.79 during canary. decode got prioritized more often.

Yuki Sato: that matches the hypothesis: fp8 attention reduces decode cost a bit, scheduler then keeps decode flowing and prefill waits longer -> TTFT up.
we probably need the scheduler knob change (batching window/backpressure) to ship alongside.

Rafael Mendes: makes sense. but for now, canary safety did its job.

Perf Canary Bot: Rollback completed for pcb-77319.
- Flag: runtime.fp8_attention_kernels
- Scope: hosted-inference / eu-west / rw-llama3-70b
- Status: reverted to `off`
- Post-rollback TTFT p95 (5m): 421ms (within +2.7% of baseline)

Rafael Mendes: great. 
@Hiro Tanaka @Yuki Sato can you take the triage? recommend: reproduce with the exact eu-west concurrency mix + check scheduler interaction. we can also route canary away from `gpu-euw-03` if driver mismatch is real.

Hiro Tanaka: yep. we’ll pull the case into the fp8/int8 regression playbook flow. can we get an nsys capture for the top 1-2 prompt buckets from eu-west?

Allison Grant: canary runner has the nsys hook now; I can schedule a capture for the exact shape bucket (long prefill / short decode) and drop artifacts in the sprint folder.

Rafael Mendes: :thumbsup: please do.
I’m also posting a short summary to #eng-runtime so it’s in their daily triage.

Vanessa Ortiz: I’ll confirm driver/CUDA versions in eu-west clusters + report back. if mismatch, we should mark eu-west as "no-fp8-canary" until pinned.

Rafael Mendes: closing the loop here once we have the infra confirmation. for now: override stays, no customer impact observed beyond the brief canary cohort.
